programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: The endearing pangolin is a little-known scaly mammal. Found in Africa and Asia, these shy creatures have an unfortunate tagline - they are the most poached and illegally trafficked animals in the world. Based in Namibia, conservationist Maria Diekmann rescues and rehabilitates her local pangolins. In a bid to better understand the global issues they are facing, we follow Maria to Vietnam, Thailand and China into the very heart of the crisis, where demand for pangolin products is greatest. In what turns out to be an emotional journey, Maria joins forces with a Chinese megastar to build a campaign to bring awareness to the plight of an animal most people have never even heard of.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Timeshift digs into the archive to discover the unwritten rules that have governed the way we drink in Britain. In the pubs and working men's clubs of the 40s and 50s there were strict customs governing who stood where. To be invited to sup at the bar was a rite of passage for many young men, and it took years for women to be accepted into these bastions of masculinity. As the country prospered and foreign travel became widely available, so new drinking habits were introduced as we discovered wine and, even more exotically, cocktails. People began to drink at home as well as at work, where journalists typified a tradition of the liquid lunch. Advertising played its part as lager was first sold as a woman's drink and then the drink of choice for young men with a bit of disposable income. The rules changed and changed again, but they were always there - unwritten and unspoken, yet underwriting our complicated relationship with drinking.

programme.title: BBC Young Musician
programme.desc: The live auditions continue, and the judges face tough decisions about who to put through to the competition’s quarter-final. Making that choice are world-famous concert pianist, educator and curator Joanna MacGregor, conductor and broadcaster Ben Gernon, and guest judge trombonist Peter Moore. Peter knows only too well what it feels like to compete in BBC Young Musician, as at just 12, he became the youngest ever winner. Broadcaster and writer Petroc Trelawny presents from the live auditions filmed earlier this year at Bath Spa University. Featuring the best young classical musicians from across the UK playing a range of instruments, from marimba to bassoon, piano to French horn, cello to clarinet. We hear music from Mozart, Liszt and Elgar, together with musical treats from lesser-known composers. At the end of the programme, the judges reveal the names of the eight musicians they want to see and hear again in the next round. Five places will be the representatives from each instrumental family - keyboard, strings, wind, brass and percussion - and three wildcard places are also up for grabs. With so much talent on display, who has done enough to get through to the quarter-final?

programme.title: Talking Shakespeare
programme.desc: Celia Imrie takes a trip through the BBC’s archive for a celebration of the works of Shakespeare, and an exploration into how the Bard’s biggest plays have been brought to cinema and television screens over the years. It’s a story that’s told through a selection of interviews with stars from the 1950s right up to the present day, with anecdotes and insights revealing how Shakespeare’s plays have been continuously adapted to suit each new generation, capturing changing attitudes to race and gender. Amongst those featured are the established acting knights Olivier and Gielgud, dames Helen Mirren, Judi Dench and Maggie Smith, and the latest wave of big names, including David Tennant, David Harewood and Maxine Peake.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: With an acting career that started in the 1970s, Lesley Manville is an established star of stage and screen, with TV roles ranging from Emmerdale to Harlots, films such as High Hopes and Phantom Thread, and a stage career ranging from the RSC to the forefront of British writing at the famous Royal Court theatre. She is perfectly placed to tell us about Caryl Churchill’s Top Girls, a play that quickly established itself as a landmark in British theatre. In 1982, she was part of the original cast, a production that garnered awards and a Broadway transfer. In 1991, she played the lead in a BBC version helmed by the show’s original director, Max Stafford Clark. Lesley tells us about her memories of the original stage show - how a cast that included Gwen Taylor and Lyndsay Duncan came to be aware of the power of what they were involved in. She explains some of the themes behind Churchill’s writing, the rise of Thatcherism and the impact it had on feminism. She discusses the cast, her memories of filming and the difference between acting the piece on stage as opposed to TV. But mostly, she reinforces the legacy of Churchill’s work, not just in this country but around the world.

programme.title: Performance
programme.desc: Seven actresses take sixteen roles in this uncompromising assessment of high-profile and low-profile women, part fantasy, part hard-nosed reality. Marlene celebrates her new position as managing director of the Top Girls Appointment Agency by giving a dinner party for five oddly assorted women from centuries past. But Marlene's own past will throw a question mark over her Top Girls success. Author Caryl Churchill describes her play as 'a celebration of the extraordinary achievements of women'.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.desc: Portrait of Caryl Churchill, one of Britain's most prolific and versatile playwrights. Featuring extracts from her plays.

programme.title: Shakespeare in Italy
programme.desc: Francesco da Mosto takes to the Italian road again in search of Shakespeare in Italy. From Romeo and Juliet to the jealousy of Othello, Shakespeare used the land of love to tell his most passionate stories about falling in love. Needless to say, along the way Francesco adds some insights of his own and revels in claims that not only did Shakespeare visit Italy, but also was born in Sicily. It's a whole new take on the Bard!

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.desc: Isolated since the time of the dinosaurs, New Zealand's wildlife has been left to its own devices, with surprising consequences. Its ancient forests are still stalked by predators from the Jurassic era. It's also one of the most geologically active countries on earth. From Kiwis with their giant eggs, to forest-dwelling penguins and helicopter-riding sheep dogs, meet the astonishing creatures and resilient people who must rise to the challenges of their beautiful, dramatic and demanding home.

programme.title: Art of France
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon explores how art in France took a dramatic turn following the French Revolution that ushered in a bold new world. From the execution of King Louis XVI and the rise of Napoleon Bonaparte - a figure who simultaneously repelled and inspired artists of his time - through to the rise of Romanticism and an art of seduction, sex and high drama, Andrew explores artists including Jacques-Louis David - whose art appeared on the barricades and in the streets - as well as the work of Delacroix, Ingres and the tragic but brilliant Theodore Gericault.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci
programme.desc: Leonardo works as a military engineer, designs fanciful flying machines, studies light and shadow, investigates gravity, dissects cadavers and pens treatises on a vast array of subjects, all while seeking the perfect patron. In Florence, Milan, Rome and finally France, he pours the sum of his scientific and artistic knowledge into a portrait that will become the most famous painting on earth. A film by Ken Burns, Sarah Burns and David McMahon.

programme.title: Ancient Worlds
programme.desc: In Richard Miles's epic story of civilization, there have been plenty of examples of the great men of history, but none came close to the legend of Alexander of Macedon, known to us as 'the Great'. Uniting the fractious Greek city-states, he led them on a crusade against the old enemy, Persia, and in little more than a decade created an empire that stretched from Egypt in the west to Afghanistan in the east. But it was Alexander's successors, the Hellenistic Kings, who had to make sense of the legacy of this charismatic adventurer. By knuckling down to the hard graft of politics, taxation and public works, they created something far more enduring than a mere legend - they built a civilization. Richard traces Alexander's battle-scarred route through Turkey, Syria and Lebanon to Egypt and ultimately to the western Punjab, Pakistan, where he discovers fascinating traces of a city where Greek west and Buddhist east were united in an intriguing new way.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: Ask E. Jean – Storyville tells the extraordinary story of journalist, author and advice columnist E. Jean Carroll, whose irreverent wit, fearless spirit and determination have defined a career spanning more than five decades. Now, she is also known as the woman who took on President Donald Trump. This film looks at her early days as Miss Cheerleader USA to how she became a pioneering voice in American magazine journalism. Carroll broke new ground as the first female editor at Esquire, Playboy and Outside, challenging conventions and helping redefine women’s role in the media. The film charts her remarkable professional achievements and the legal battle against President Donald Trump (who was out of office at the time) that brought her international attention. Carroll sued Trump twice in the civil courts over sexual abuse and defamation allegations - and won both times, transforming a deeply personal fight into a broader conversation about truth, justice and accountability.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Sandra Maksimovic reports from Serbia, where a deadly infrastructure disaster has become the catalyst for the country's biggest political challenge in years. What began as a demand for accountability has grown into a nationwide student-led protest movement against corruption, exposing deep divisions over governance, transparency and Serbia's future direction. As the country heads to the polls, we examine a nation increasingly divided between competing visions of what Serbia is and what it should become. Plus: the growing debate over AI safety. How realistic are warnings that artificial intelligence could pose an existential threat to humanity?

programme.title: Clive Myrie's African Adventure
programme.desc: The second leg of Clive’s adventure takes him to Durban, known for its fabulous surfing beaches and chilled atmosphere. It’s also the biggest city in the spectacular KwaZulu-Natal province, ancestral home of the Zulu people. Clive jumps into action as he joins an anti-poaching team saving South Africa’s critically endangered rhinos from extinction and joins a surf school that teaches homeless and disadvantaged kids the skills to surf – and to transform their lives. Back in the city, Clive gets a lesson in making spicy bunny chow, the iconic street food created by Durban’s large Indian population, before heading out to the Valley of a Thousand Hills for a masterclass in Zulu beadwork at a craft centre that gives women living with HIV the skills to support their families.

programme.desc: Record-high diesel prices caused by the wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered rising unrest across Europe. Plus, the CEO of Burmester Audiosysteme, Thorsten Poenig, explains the challenges of selling German technology in China.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp and the teams shop for antiques in Nottinghamshire with experts Ben Cooper and Izzie Balmer, before heading to Derby for today’s auction. Natasha discovers how one publisher from the Regency period started a brand new toy craze.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc: Aled Jones and the Rev Kate Bottley present the senior semi-final of BBC Young Chorister of the Year at Hallé St Peter’s in Manchester. Songs of Praise and BBC Radio 2 have joined forces to showcase the country’s best young vocal talents, and five fantastic singers aged 15 to 17 have chosen a sacred song to impress this year’s judges, David Grant, Laura Wright and Cameron Richardson. Music choices include Pie Jesu from Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Requiem, Rejoice Greatly from Handel’s Messiah, Caccini’s Ave Maria, the hymn I Cannot Tell and For All the Saints Who’ve Shown Your Love by contemporary composer John Bell. The singers come together to perform Morning Has Broken, arranged by composer Helen Leach. After all the choristers have sung, the judges will select three singers to progress to the final.

programme.title: Shrek the Third
programme.desc: Second sequel in the popular animated fantasy franchise. Newlyweds Shrek and Fiona face their first marital hurdle when the sudden death of King Harold means Shrek himself is next in line. However, with fatherhood looming, Shrek is reluctant. He decides to try and find the true heir - Fiona's errant, rebellious cousin. But while Shrek and his faithful companions Donkey and Puss in Boots go off in search of the heir, handsome rogue Prince Charming stages a coup at the castle. Featuring the voices of Mike Myers (Shrek), Eddie Murphy (Donkey), Cameron Diaz (Princess Fiona), Antonio Banderas (Puss in Boots), Julie Andrews (Queen Lillian), John Cleese (King Harold), Rupert Everett (Prince Charming), Eric Idle (Merlin), Justin Timberlake (Artie), John Krasinski (Lancelot), Ian McShane (Captain Hook) and Amy Poehler (Snow White).

programme.title: Kingdom
programme.desc: An injured wild dog, Flint, needs the support of his pack more than ever before. But in return he helps to care for Storm’s largest litter of puppies to date, revealing a new and surprising side to wild dogs. A showdown between mother and daughter sees leopard Olimba struggling to keep a grip on her territory, while Mutima roams Nsefu searching for a new home. The fragmented hyena clan is reuniting and rebuilding its strength, but so is the lion pride. Another shift in the balance of power seems inevitable, until the pride is confronted by elemental forces outside its control.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Jacqui is not impressed by the mushrooms growing inside a Norfolk end-of-terrace. In the West Midlands, Dion thinks some walls need to be rebuilt. And Martel loves the story behind how a foster father and his son paired up as property developers.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita Rani and Sean Fletcher head to the south Pennines to join archaeologists and conservationists uncovering the remarkable ways peat is preserving our past while helping to protect our future. Meanwhile, John Craven reveals the winner of this year’s Countryfile photography competition for Children in Need.

programme.title: The Reluctant Vampire
programme.desc: Val has to come up with a plan to pass the vampire initiation ceremony despite his huge secret. However, his curiosity about human life gets the better of him, and he sneaks to the village, where he bumps into Gertie and is thrust straight into human family life. His two worlds collide when he’s invited to a party.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s time for the latest round of results as the couples wait to find out if they’ve secured a place in the next theme week - icons. The pros attempt to settle once and for all whether ballroom or Latin dancing is best in the professional group number as Shirley and Anton go head-to-head in the ultimate dance battle. There’s music from Jalen Ngonda, and two more couples must perform again for the last remaining place in the competition. Whose time in the ballroom has run out?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at picturesque Dartington Estate near Totnes in Devon. Duncan Campbell is entranced by an 18th-century sundial compass and the story of its heroic owner, while Ronnie Archer-Morgan discovers how a bush pilot was saved by an African tribe and gifted a traditional headrest. Elaine Binning is intrigued by a walking stick with a secret gadget hidden inside, while Richard Price hears how a valuable Rolex watch was almost thrown out with the rubbish. Chris Yeo flexes his muscles with a piece of vintage mail order gym kit, and Hilary Kay is thrilled to find an early 20th-century Jemima Puddle-duck doll inspired by Beatrix Potter. Fiona Bruce explores the history of the estate, home to Leonard and Dorothy Elmhirst and the 'Dartington experiment', which made it a haven for artists, writers and thinkers in the early 20th century. Alex Aguilar challenges Fiona to pick the odd one out from three pieces of ancient ceramics.

programme.title: Time
programme.desc: New chaplain Marie-Louise arrives at the young offender institution HMYOI Alderwick and finds herself immediately at odds with traditionalist and world-weary custodial manager Bailey, who is dealing with his own personal crisis. They lock horns over how to handle Christopher, a young man with a stammer who has recently reconnected with his birth mother. Meanwhile, Peter and his friends arrive at the prison after being involved in an attack on a man, and James is relocated from another prison.

programme.title: Match of the Day

programme.title: The Nice Guys

programme.title: The Graham Norton Show

programme.title: Crimewatch Live
programme.desc: In 1988, Lee Boxell disappeared after seeing a friend. His heartbroken family are still looking for him. Plus, justice for the man jailed 14 years after he attacked three women.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: A flat in an old mill building just outside Manchester impresses Martel. In west London, Jacqui spots a property with potential to extend, while Dion’s loving life in Lincolnshire at a mixed residential and commercial opportunity.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: See if you can beat fairgoers as they try to guess the purpose of Eric’s mystery object. It’s made of a hard wood and has a screw top with holes pierced in it. All will be revealed! At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, the teams keep Eric guessing what they bought until their 60 minutes is up. Shopping with expert Lesley Kiddell-Spencer are friends and PhD students Harriet and Alice, who plan to use logic and charm to get a deal, and with Irita Marriott are dad and daughter AJ and Jiya. He's looking for watches, and she’s after silver and jewellery. Can the students dial in a profit when they come across a stall of upcycled telephones, or can AJ and Jiya make them green with envy if they buy a Blue John pendant? There are certainly plenty of intriguing items to tempt the bidders at Hettie Jago’s sale room in Nottingham, but will this contest come down to the bonus buys at the end of the show?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: Mark Wright and his team, Karla Pryce and Asher Edwards, take on Robin’s chaotic one-bedroom basement flat. Robin, a single dad with ADHD, has struggled to manage his precious personal belongings, which have overwhelmed his space. Karla works tirelessly to declutter, create systems and tidy up the living room and bedroom. Asher repurposes old furniture, builds custom storage and crafts a new desk for Robin’s arts and crafts. By the end of the transformation, Robin’s flat is a functional, organised haven for both him and his son.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc: In Bridgend, Anum and Betti race to turn charity shop finds into profit, risking big on designer items, bold upcycles and a high-stakes live-streamed auction.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Three generations, one big move and a lot of opinions! Alistair Appleton is in Cornwall, helping an extended family from a Buckinghamshire town find a rural home with room for everyone. His mystery house is a beautiful conversion packed with possibilities. Away from the house hunt, Alistair meets a pair of talented locals shining a light on the Cornish landscape with their handcrafted lamps.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo and Sue are in Stevenage to help mother and daughter Margaret and Elizabeth transform their south-facing garden. While blessed with sunlight, the space is currently a chaotic jumble of mismatched plant pots, overgrown bushes and uneven, sloped steps, making it overwhelming and difficult to enjoy. Their dream is to turn it into a mother–daughter retreat with a serene, shaded relaxation garden. Elizabeth and Margaret envision a charming pergola draped in delicate vines, offering a peaceful spot to unwind together. Wider, gently sloping steps and accessible raised beds will allow Margaret to continue her beloved gardening safely, while lush, in-ground plants reduce maintenance. They also hope for privacy screening and planting that discreetly hides the shed at the back of the garden. Elizabeth juggles a demanding full-time job with caring for her ageing mother, leaving little time to work on the garden. Margaret is retired and longing to enjoy the outdoors, but her partial sight makes the current low-lying plants and treacherous steps a real obstacle to relaxation and upkeep. Can the team turn this challenging plot into a peaceful mother–daughter retreat on a £4,500 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this quiz show where a team of four friends Karen, Andrew, Mary and Arwel take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Andi Oliver for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Ned rallies the community to celebrate becoming co-owner of Harry's Barn. Lauren and Mark's secret threatens to catch up with them. Amy finds herself increasingly drawn to Craig.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Roman Abramovich was the UK’s most famous oligarch, the Russian billionaire who helped Chelsea win the Champions League. New evidence from an offshore data leak suggests his business empire was built on lies. Working with the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, Panorama has uncovered hundreds of documents which appear to have been falsified and backdated to conceal his vast fortune. Reporter Richard Bilton investigates Roman Abramovich’s suspect paperwork and the big accountancy firm which signed off his misleading accounts. Roman Abramovich disputes the allegations and denies any wrongdoing.

programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey travels to Florida to meet fitness influencer and T-maxxer Adam Katz. He’s part of a wave of young men boosting their testosterone to get pumped bodies and appear as manly as possible to the opposite sex. But this boost might just be skin-deep, as Stacey explores evidence suggesting long-term use can permanently lower your sperm count and even risks shrinking your testicles. She then discovers that this particular social craze may not be so modern after all as she follows a trail that leads her to Wolverhampton Wanderers and a bizarre revelation that the FA Cup final in 1939 was nicknamed the 'Monkey Gland Final' after several players had testosterone-boosting injections before the game. Migraines can be so severe that they trigger headaches and vomiting that last for hours, so Stacey is intrigued by a social trend that claims they can be cured by a fast food meal. She explores with the doctors if there could be a kernel of scientific truth in the claims.

programme.title: Time
programme.desc: Officer Bailey faces a moral crossroads after tragedy strikes HMYOI Alderwick, whilst Marie-Louise and the governor deliver some news to family on the outside. James, consumed by shame, learns a truth and debates facing family he has been avoiding. Peter’s guilt inside grows, and he forms an unlikely connection. Pressure hits a critical high at the prison as officers and prisoners alike struggle to cope.

programme.desc: Mark Wright and his team, Asher Edwards and Maxine Dwyer, help single mum Sammy reclaim her home from the chaos of clutter and create a more functional space. Overtaken by toys, Sammy's living room lacks a dedicated area for relaxation, and her bedroom has a mattress on the floor. The team work hard to reorganise the living room, build custom storage and give Sammy’s bedroom a much-needed makeover. With a new bed frame, decluttered space and clever zoning, Sammy can finally relax and enjoy her home.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this quiz show where a family team of four, Kezia, Nathaniel, Seyi and Femi, take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die. As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated. Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death. Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales. Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height.

programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Stacey travels to Florida to meet fitness influencer and T-maxxer Adam Katz. He’s part of a wave of young men boosting their testosterone to get pumped bodies and appear as manly as possible to the opposite sex. But this boost might just be skin-deep, as Stacey explores evidence suggesting long-term use can permanently lower your sperm count and even risks shrinking your testicles. She then discovers that this particular social craze may not be so modern after all as she follows a trail that leads her to Wolverhampton Wanderers and a bizarre revelation that the FA Cup final in 1939 was nicknamed the 'Monkey Gland Final' after several players had testosterone-boosting injections before the game. Migraines can be so severe that they trigger headaches and vomiting that last for hours, so Stacey is intrigued by a social trend that claims they can be cured by a fast food meal. She explores with the doctors if there could be a kernel of scientific truth in the claims.

programme.title: Wisdom of the Crowd

programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May attempt to prove that the hot hatchbacks of their youth were better than their modern equivalents by buying a 'classic' example of the breed each and then undertaking a series of challenges. programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: The series continues with a jam-packed show featuring Italian sports cars, military manoeuvres and a trip to Belgium. Richard Hammond is on the shores of Lake Como testing the exciting new Alfa Romeo 4C, a mid-engined machine from one of the world's most beloved sports car makers. Hammond's enjoyment of the super-lightweight, 237-horsepower beauty is brought to an abrupt halt by the arrival of Jeremy Clarkson on a quad bike, demanding a race to the far end of the vast lake. Unfortunately for Hammond, Clarkson's quad bike is not entirely as it first seems. Elsewhere in the programme, Clarkson is in the genteel surroundings of Bruges, and at the rather less sedate Spa Grand Prix track in order to test a thrilling new breed of hybrid hypercar: the stunning 904-horsepower McLaren P1. Meanwhile, James May is at the vast Camp Bastion in Afghanistan looking at the incredible efforts behind the army's largest vehicle redeployment since the Second World War. programme.title: Hyperdrive
programme.desc: The year is 2151, and Commander Henderson and the crew of HMS Camden Lock are protecting Britain's interests in a changing galaxy. That means persuading alien cultures to move their businesses to the Peterborough enterprise zone. This would be difficult enough if there wasn't a lethal, man-eating parasite loose on the ship. Which there is.

programme.title: Hyperdrive
programme.desc: Commander Henderson and his crew are making first contact with the alien civilisation of Queppu. The first rule of first contact is: never, ever get romantically involved with a beautiful alien princess. So Henderson falls head over heels in love. Meanwhile, the ship has been left in the sole charge of Technical Officer Jeffers. Big mistake.

programme.title: Hyperdrive
programme.desc: Everyone on board the spaceship HMS Camden Lock has the weekend off to mark Gary Neville Day - the holiday celebrating the 21st-century footballer and inventor of artificial gravity. Vine has just bought an entire planet in an internet auction. He insists it was a bargain and not the useless, poisonous ball of clay it appears to be. Teal is looking forward to dining with Henderson at the Officers' Dinner - perhaps a little bit too much.

programme.title: Hyperdrive
programme.desc: Sci-fi comedy set aboard the spaceship HMS Camden Lock. The ship is hosting delicate peace talks between the Lallakkiss and the Bulaahg, two feuding alien species. When Henderson deploys his ingenuity and charm to hurry things along, the species unite and declare war on Britain. With Starbase unwilling to send back-up, it's the Camden Lock against 900 enemy ships.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC New Comedy Awards are back. Over 1,200 applied before being whittled down to the top 30 comics. In this episode, five hopefuls battle it out for a place in the grand final in Cardiff, where one of them will be crowned the BBC New Comedian of 2022. This show comes from The Albany, Deptford – a charity and social enterprise that has been supporting the people of Lewisham for over 125 years. The Albany has a long association with comedy. Vic Reeves and Bob Mortimer kicked off their careers in what was then the Albany Empire. Hosting the show is local award-winning stand-up and actress Thanyia Moore. Joining Thanyia is actress and stand-up Kerry Godliman and rising star Babatunde Aleshe, winner of the Best Newcomer at the Black Entertainer Comedy awards. Keeping the house in order is head judge Fern Brady, who brings her honest and authentic approach to judging as only Fern can. The judges will have a tough job picking a winner from the five new comics who will take to the stage with material jam-packed with fresh topics and jokes aplenty.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc: Invited into the traditionally private Gypsy community, Stacey discovers the complex balancing act young women face growing up in one of Britain’s most maligned ethnic minorities.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: Dr David Graham is online and looking for love. He seems to have it all: the looks, the job, and the charisma. On paper, he’s Kilmarnock’s most eligible bachelor. But when the town’s former beauty queen Abbie Draper starts to receive messages from him after he treats her grandfather in hospital, she gets the feeling he might be too good to be true. She turns online sleuth and starts to uncover a trail of deception, crazy coincidences and stories that just don’t add up. Dr David isn’t just a bad boyfriend; something more sinister is afoot. Abbie starts trying to figure out who David Graham really is and why he is doing this.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: Dr David’s victims begin comparing their stories, and it becomes clear they are dealing with a sophisticated catfish. But nothing could prepare them for the shocking truth of the perpetrator’s true identity, which leaves the women with more questions than answers. But when beauty queen Abbie takes these findings to the police, they are unable to do anything about it, and the Catfish of Kilmarnock remains free to target more and more victims. Abbie can’t walk away, and steps up her investigation over months that turn into years. As she continues to track the catfish, the scale of their criminality comes into focus, with victims spread across the country and dating back over a decade. This is one of the UK’s most prolific ever catfish, and they are not done yet.

programme.title: The Beauty Queen and the Catfish
programme.desc: As criminal investigations take hold, the victims finally have justice, but they are still left urgently searching for answers as they try to rebuild their lives. What drives someone, with a seemingly normal life, to throw it all away to terrorise countless women from the same town? With no clear motive and no explanation from the person in the frame, this very modern true crime tale now turns to those closest to the perpetrator, who are also trying to understand the mystery behind the repeated cycles of offending. As the beauty queen and the catfish’s lives become ever more entangled, lines begin to blur, loyalties are tested, and Abbie finds herself questioning everything as history repeats, and the moral complexity of crime and punishment in the internet age is laid bare. For the many victims, the question remains: what drives someone to become one of the UK’s most prolific catfish - and why can’t they stop?

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: The nation grew up with Top of the Pops, and it was always a talking point, but 35 years ago, a particular kind of Top of the Pops programme and tone held sway. This documentary explores Top of the Pops in 1976 - as a barometer of the state of pop and light entertainment TV. It celebrates the power of the programme and observes the British society of the mid-70s, British TV and the British pop scene. In 1976, glam was over and nothing had replaced it - the charts belonged to Showaddywaddy, Brotherhood of Man and The Wurzels, all to be found on Top of the Pops hosted by the Radio 1 DJs. If you wanted rock, you looked to the Old Grey Whistle Test, while outside the charts, a new scene was rumbling. Contributors include Tony Blackburn, David 'Diddy' Hamilton, Paul Morley, Toyah Willcox, Showaddywaddy, Brotherhood of Man, The Wurzels and Dave Haslam.

programme.title: Brief History of a Family
programme.desc: Psychological drama. Enigmatic 15-year-old Yan Shuo is injured in an accident caused by Tu Wei, a classmate from an affluent family. Wei invites Shuo to his house, where he impresses the Tu family and begins to feel at home. In Mandarin with English subtitles.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Emily McGowan are in the Cotswolds for the biggest date in the sheepdog trialling calendar - the Supreme. The finest dogs and handlers from across the UK and Ireland go head-to-head in a thrilling showcase of instinct, skill and control. After months of training and a year of tough qualifying trials, it all comes down to this - but only one will claim the coveted title of Supreme Champion.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Easter Ross on the shores of the Cromarty Firth, where he meets the couple sowing their seed-growing business in the area’s fertile farmland. Cammy is in Angus to hear how award-winning beef farmers made the switch back to native cattle for better results. Meanwhile, Rachel continues her journey round the Buchan Coast for a lesson making fishing nets, Arlene heads to the Isle of Jura to find out how three women are making a living and living their dream, and Dougie uncloaks the hidden story of a familiar local landmark.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek is on a mission to find his best west Walian walks - he has 17 years' worth to choose from! For his first flashback, Derek is in Cardigan Bay, where he discovers the legend of Cantre’r Gwaelod at Sarn Cynfelyna. Derek also has a go at stand-up paddle-boarding, before finishing at the university town of Aberystwyth. On his second walk, Derek travels to Ceredigion, walking from Bwlch yr Arian, where he feeds red kites, to Devil’s Bridge, famed for its three stacked bridges. On the way, he discovers the silver and lead mining history of the area. Finally, Derek follows the course of the River Teifi between Cenarth and Cilgerran, where he learns to steer a coracle, the area’s ancient form of fishing boat, and takes part in the annual coracle races.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt serves up a feast of global flavours from favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Mike Reid serves up a classic Parisian bistro dish of steak frites with a traditional Parisian sauce, while Donal Skehan and Donna Hay whip up a light and fluffy gnocchi (or gnudi) with a fresh cherry tomato and ricotta sauce. Jack Croft and Will Murray break down how to master the art of the perfect chicken wings, Shivi Ramoutar prepares curry crab and dumplings, and Paul A Young demonstrates how to make chocolate from scratch. Finally, Hollywood superstar Stanley Tucci tucks into a choice of two food heavens at the end of the show - a traditional venison bolognese or a vibrant crown prince risotto. Meanwhile, Rick Stein heads to an infamous pudding club for an astonishing seven puddings, and the Hairy Bikers head to the picturesque salt flats of France.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Starting in the port city of Marseilles, Eva shares a spicy half-and-half pizza with local chef and rising star Valentin Ruffali, before heading to La Ola to try a delicious blend of French and north African cuisine courtesy of chef Khouloude Ben Thayer. After enjoying the ancient and feted bouillabaisse fish broth, Eva heads out into the sun-kissed landscape to try the traditional summer vegetable dish of ratatouille and a sun-drenched salad niçoise on the Riviera at the famous Hotel du Cap.

programme.title: Nigel and Adam's Farm Kitchen
programme.desc: In this final episode, Nigel and Adam look at Britain's heritage foods - the old favourites still on our shopping lists today - and how the way they are cooked and who eats them has changed over the years. With pigs having historically provided food for British families all year round, and with every county in the country still rearing pigs, pork in its many forms, from ham to bacon and sausages, is the most popular choice of meat. So how do farmers meet our demands for pork? The boys find out by rearing their own three different breeds of pig. As the series draws to a close, Adam takes to the markets to sell off the produce to raise funds for Children in Need.

programme.title: The Ipcress File
programme.desc: Spy thriller in which intelligence agent Harry Palmer is plunged into the shabby and treacherous world of counter-espionage as he uncovers a bizarre brain drain among scientists. Based on the novel by Len Deighton.

programme.title: Funeral in Berlin
programme.desc: Harry Palmer is sent to Berlin with instructions to assist Colonel Stok, the Russian head of security for the Berlin Wall, who is eager to defect to the West. However, Palmer discovers he cannot trust anyone in the city where the double-cross is a unit of currency.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: A new year begins, bringing new life and new experiences. Carianne and her brother-in-law Alexander take Faillish the bull to the Oban Highland Show, hoping to bag a rosette and sell him for a good price. But Carianne is nervous about being in charge. In South Ayrshire, lambing starts early with a flock of pedigree Suffolks. It’s all hands to the pump for the whole family, with the twins Cameron and Finlay rising early to help out before school. For Rachel and Camy in Inverkip, the time has come to scan their ewes to see how many are pregnant – a big moment of truth for their fledgling breeding programme. But first they must navigate the hills surrounding Dunrod Farm to find them all.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! makes Leicester's De Montfort Hall its home, and the experts hunting out the best antiques and collectables to take to auction are Claire Rawle and Thomas Plant. Paul Martin discovers a collection of Picasso ceramics put together by a legend in his own right - Lord Richard Attenborough.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: National treasure Moira Stuart and star of stage and screen Aled Jones go head-to-head in a battle of antiques in Kent. Swapping the studio for the road, they cruise around in an all-electric Porsche 911. Helping hands on this trip are antique gurus David Harper and Serhat Ahmet. Moira shocks and surprises David with her eclectic, unorthodox choices and haggling tactics, while Aled and Serhat find common ground over sport and music. They squeeze in a stop at the town of Sandwich to hear the story of a medieval battle that would certainly have made the news, then it’s off to auction for a saleroom showdown. Who will make headline winners and who will be singing for their supper?

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Bordeaux’s world-famous vineyards are undergoing a revival as vintners seek to update their wines by introducing new technology and reinventing older traditions. Eva visits Saint-Emilion, where wine production began 1,000 years ago, and enjoys unusual wine pairings - a deep red with fish and a buttery white with cheese. But Bordeaux isn’t just about wine; it has superb produce, including succulent duck and tender beef as well as 200-million-year-old caviar, served with signature bordelaise sauces.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims' final destination is Bardsey Island, the fabled ‘Island of 20,000 Saints’. Along the way, they see spectacular landscapes, visit holy sites and engage in fasting, ritual and meditation.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve journeys deep into Canada’s vast and empty Yukon territory – one of North America’s most iconic and remote landscapes. Covering an area almost the size of Spain but home to fewer than 50,000 people, the Yukon is a land of immense forests, glaciers, rivers and wildlife. In wealthy, modern Canada, Simon wants to find out how the people and the wildlife of this immense wilderness are faring - all while searching for an apex predator, the grizzly bear.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools is joined by Paul Heaton, Skye Newman, DC3, mary in the junkyard and Dermot Henry, and chats to Johnny Marr.

programme.title: Don't Look Now
programme.desc: Grieving the loss of their young daughter in a tragic accident, Laura and John Baxter visit Venice, where John is helping to restore a dilapidated church. As John works, Laura is befriended by two sisters, one of whom warns them to leave the city, claiming she has seen their dead daughter. Classic mystery thriller from Nicolas Roeg.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: After receiving a Cameo birthday message from one of his comedy heroes, Nigel Planer, Lee does not realise that Lucy has paid for it. So, when he sees Nigel in a packed restaurant, he rushes over to introduce himself, assuming that they must now be best friends. This is news to Nigel.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Peterlee in County Durham, with politicians, commentators and members of the public. On the panel are, from the government, the justice minister Jake Richards; the Conservative shadow Scottish secretary Harriet Cross; Max Wilkinson from the Liberal Democrats; the Daily Mirror’s associate editor Kevin Maguire; and the Telegraph’s senior political commentator Annabel Denham.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: In Watergate Bay, one of Cornwall’s surfing hotspots, two teenage boys are caught in one of the beach’s notorious rip currents. When three distress signals are activated off the Pembrokeshire coast, the Fishguard crew race out to their location; en route, they discover there are seven kayakers in need of rescue, with winds gusting at 50 miles an hour. On one of the hottest days of the year, the Lyme Regis crew receive reports of a man suffering from heat stroke on a remote stretch of beach. And on the Isle of Wight, a fossil hunter is trapped waist deep in mud - with the tide steadily rising.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Indulge in a splash of seaside nostalgia with host Caroline Hawley and two more teams of antiques hunters. In Bristol, Caroline visits the Martin Parr Foundation to view a genre-defining exhibition by the late photographer Martin Parr CBE. It’s 40 years since Parr produced his iconic collection of images of working-class family holidays in the Merseyside resort of New Brighton. Parr’s radical style broke away from the professional black-and-white photography of the time, earning him both praise and criticism for his colour-rich images. Aiming to snap up bargains of their own in Warwickshire are two teams of family and friends. In red are pals and amateur actors David and Shawn with antiques expert David Fergus, and in blue are father and daughter-in-law Ollie and Perdie with their expert Thomas Forrester. With an hour to shop, the reds wonder if they’ll squeeze out a profit with a wooden juicer, while the blues decide whether a 1970s first-aid kit will remedy their challenge. In the saleroom, there are ups and downs for both teams until the bidders take a shine to one particular polished purchase.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Architect duo Rob and Alfonso take on the task of restoring their historic terraced house into a stylish, contemporary home. Can they achieve their dream of creating a unique home and workspace with the perfect balance of old and new? Presented by Hugh Wallace.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Mark Chapman presents highlights of three Premier League games as well as September’s Goal of the Month. Manchester City face Liverpool in a highly charged fixture at Anfield, newly promoted Hull City are looking to continue their impressive start to the season at home to unbeaten Everton, and Nottingham Forest travel to Crystal Palace, who are so far without a win in the Premier League.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: The Boss
programme.desc: Susan Calman hosts the quiz show of tactics, knowledge and nerve. Contestants must work as a team, but ultimately there can only be one Boss. Who will pick off their opponents and walk away with the thousands of pounds on offer?

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo begins a railway tour of the spectacular border counties of Cumbria and Dumfriesshire, starting in the stunning Lake District National Park, where he discovers the violent geological history of volcanoes and colliding continents that shaped this breathtaking landscape. For an aerial view, he takes to the skies in a gyroplane - part plane, part helicopter. In Ambleside, at the National School of Forestry, Michael meets the trainees aspiring to become qualified foresters, and a visit to the heritage Lakeside and Haverthwaite Railway charts the region’s transformation from mining to tourism. Finally, Michael explores Sellafield, a key site in the UK’s nuclear history, and drives a train normally used to transport spent nuclear fuel across one of the largest private railway sidings in Europe.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Paul buys back his former family home and takes on the mammoth task of restoring it himself. With dry rot, a leaking roof and rotten beams standing in his way, can he save his old childhood home, and his mother’s pride and joy, from ruin? Presented by Hugh Wallace.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel takes the Roadshow to visit Mount Stewart in Northern Ireland. Treasures include a valuable painting once thrown on a skip, a memento from Laurel and Hardy, and Henry Sandon is introduced to a mug bearing his spitting image.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Ragley Hall in Warwickshire, a beautiful 17th-century Palladian house owned by the Marquess of Hertford. Antiques experts Charlie Ross and Will Axon find great treasures among hundreds of visitors to the stately home. Charlie models an interesting Busby hat and Will gets a surprise when a Worcester coffee set goes under the hammer. Paul Martin explores the Battle of Edgehill.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chizzy Akudolu, Stephen Bailey, Banjo Beale and Philippa Dunne take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the brand new House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor has another week of behind-the-scenes exclusives and backstage Strictly gossip. She’s joined by the latest couple to be eliminated, and the panel of all-stars returns to break down all the weekend’s action.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Nadine Yousif reports from Canada, where growing tensions over Alberta's place within the federation are fuelling a debate about identity, sovereignty and political power. As some push for greater autonomy and others warn against deepening divisions, Global Eye examines competing visions of Canada's future. Plus: we travel to the remote mountains of Papua, where the world's last tropical glaciers are rapidly disappearing, exploring what their loss means for Indigenous communities and a landscape undergoing profound change.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge in another Mastermind heat. The specialist subjects are The Lord of the Rings by JRR Tolkien, the band Talking Heads, the television series Foyle's War and the PDC World Darts Championship.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Nobody goes home after this episode – that’s just how the series structure rolls. The questions are as quirky as ever, for example: what connects panorama, accountant, unalive and seggs?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The first round of the competition concludes with a match between SOAS University of London and Edinburgh. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Being Muslim After 9/11
programme.desc: After long careers exploring British Muslim life as journalists and film-makers, Mobeen Azhar and Masood Khan revisit their archive, reconnect with old interviewees and meet a wider range of people with important stories to tell, seeking to understand how things have changed for their community in the 25 years since 9/11.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob fish the beautiful river Wensum in search of the equally beautifully roach. Struggling up and down the riverbanks, they realise how age is starting to take its toll on their physicality. But Bob has a plan to help Paul recapture his youth. They stay overnight in a disused train station and visit the local pub with Paul showing off his new look, courtesy of Bob. They decide to challenge each other to a fishing competition where the winner gets a very special culinary treat, and be warned, their dinner table conversation is not for the faint hearted.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: American Fiction
programme.desc: Novelist Thelonious 'Monk' Ellison's books are well-reviewed and well-regarded, but they don't sell well, and he is in a rut. Despairing at the way other black authors are marketed and the way they're expected to write and behave, he pens a tough crime novel under a pseudonym, as a protest, expecting it to disappear. But things get out of hand when publishers love it, and his alter ego, the wanted felon Stagg R Leigh, is offered a huge advance.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Emily McGowan are in the Cotswolds for the biggest date in the sheepdog trialling calendar - the Supreme. The finest dogs and handlers from across the UK and Ireland go head-to-head in a thrilling showcase of instinct, skill and control. After months of training and a year of tough qualifying trials, it all comes down to this - but only one will claim the coveted title of Supreme Champion.

programme.title: The Celebrity Traitors
programme.desc: As the first banishment unfolds, the Faithful are hoping that they’ve caught a Traitor, while the Traitors are desperate to keep their identities concealed. The celebrities must put their trust in one another during a mission that fuels suspicion and paranoia amongst the players. When night descends, tensions rise at the Round Table. Will the players succeed in exposing a Traitor, or will an innocent Faithful be wrongfully banished?

programme.title: The Celebrity Traitors: Uncloaked
programme.desc: Ed Gamble hears from the latest banished and murdered players from episode 3 about their time in the castle, and he gets their reactions to the Traitors' identities.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: See if you can beat fairgoers as they try to guess the purpose of Eric’s mystery object. It’s made of a hard wood and has a screw top with holes pierced in it. All will be revealed! At Southwell Racecourse in Nottinghamshire, the teams keep Eric guessing what they bought until their 60 minutes is up. Shopping with expert Lesley Kiddell-Spencer are friends and PhD students Harriet and Alice, who plan to use logic and charm to get a deal, and with Irita Marriott are dad and daughter AJ and Jiya. He's looking for watches, and she’s after silver and jewellery. Can the students dial in a profit when they come across a stall of upcycled telephones, or can AJ and Jiya make them green with envy if they buy a Blue John pendant? There are certainly plenty of intriguing items to tempt the bidders at Hettie Jago’s sale room in Nottingham, but will this contest come down to the bonus buys at the end of the show?

Away from the house hunt, Alistair meets a pair of talented locals shining a light on the Cornish landscape with their handcrafted lamps.

programme.desc: In three of Derek’s top coastal rambles, he gets a dunking in Pembrokeshire, discovers why Porth Neigwl is dubbed Hell’s Mouth and meets some volunteers called the Silver Slashers.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway tour of Cumbria and Dumfriesshire continues as he travels along the scenic Cumbrian Coast Line. Just outside Egremont, he visits Florence Mine, an old iron ore mine now transformed into an arts centre that produces vibrant pigments from its haematite. In Ulverston, he discovers the cradle of Quakerism at Swarthmoor Hall, where secret meetings were once held by Quaker founder George Fox. Michael is invited to join a Quaker meeting. The journey wraps up in the Lyth Valley, where damsons are the local delicacy. Michael whips up a damson clafoutis.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Hugh meets designers Robin and Eoin on their journey to convert a Victorian schoolhouse into a chic family home. However, after delays and setbacks, can they transform this functional space into the home of their dreams? Presented by Hugh Wallace.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team head for Hastings, where amongst the treasures uncovered are a Meissen pot and a doodle by artist Augustus John. David Battie gets to break into a chest containing a wedding gift given in the 1920s, which has never been opened. Plus, the next contender vying for the title of Champion Collector, a man with a serious addiction for Punch and Judy.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the Fleet Air Arm Museum, home to an enormous collection of naval aviation history. This incredible selection of military heritage is located at HMS Heron in Yeovilton, the country's largest naval aviation base. Paul Martin is joined by experts Charlie Ross and Christina Trevanion. Members of the public arrive at the museum laden with hundreds of antiques and collectables to be valued by the Flog It! antique experts. Later in the show a number of items are sold at auction. Paul travels to London to find out about the famous Somerset scientist Thomas Young, whose incredible all-round knowledge earned him the title of polymath. With his theory of how light travels this remarkable West Country man's legacy can still be felt today.

programme.desc: Dave and Si are starting off their great adventure in Scotland, one of their favourite places in the whole world. It was on these Scottish roads that they first became best friends, and they're now returning to a place that holds very special memories for them both, the Isle of Bute.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: The Porthcawl crew’s training night is disrupted when a call comes from a dog walker who has spotted a surfer in trouble below the cliffs at nearby Rest Bay. During the peak of a cyclone known as Storm Amy, Bridlington’s lifeboat is tasked to a Dutch trawler that has lost power 13 miles off the Yorkshire coast. In Ireland, an urgent call comes in to the Crosshaven crew from a yacht taking part in a local race; on board, an elderly sailor is reported to have broken his leg. The Calshot crew face a tense search in thick fog for a motorboat with engine failure - somewhere in the busy shipping lanes of the Solent. And reports of a submerged car in the Thames put the Chiswick crew on red alert.

programme.title: John Simpson - 60 Years at the BBC
programme.desc: John Simpson looks back at his extraordinary 60-year career at the BBC - reporting on the biggest global stories of the era. In a frank, personal and revealing documentary, he reflects on the changing world he has witnessed: the revolution in Iran that seemed destined to fail, his brutal kidnapping in Beirut, the fall of the Berlin Wall, two wars in Iraq, the invasion of Afghanistan and a mind-altering trip up the Amazon. From the Broadcasting House newsroom in 1966 to World Affairs editor, he looks back at memorable encounters with inspiring leaders and cruel dictators - the figures who have shaped history, including Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Saddam Hussein, Colonel Gaddafi and Volodymyr Zelensky. The programme also features his insights into the role of the BBC today and the challenges faced in the age of fake news.

M.K. joins a race of beings known as the Leafmen in their battle to protect their queen (Beyoncé Knowles) from their enemies, evil Mandrake (Christoph Waltz) and his crew of Boggans.

programme.title: Mojave

programme.title: Life of Pi

Tragedy strikes when a terrible storm sinks the ship, leaving the Patels' teenage son, Pi, as the only human survivor. However, Pi is not alone; a fearsome Bengal tiger has also found refuge aboard the lifeboat. As days turn into weeks and weeks drag into months, Pi and the tiger must learn to trust each other if both are to survive.

programme.title: Pan
programme.desc: Living a bleak existence at a London orphanage, 12-year-old Peter finds himself whisked away to the fantastical world of Neverland. Adventure awaits as he meets new friend James Hook and the warrior Tiger Lily. They must band together to save Neverland from the ruthless pirate Blackbeard.

programme.title: X-Men: First Class
programme.desc: In the early 1960s, during the height of the Cold War, a mutant named Charles Xavier (James McAvoy) meets a fellow mutant named Erik Lehnsherr (Michael Fassbender). Despite their vastly different backgrounds -- Charles grew up with a wealthy family, while Erik lost his parents at Auschwitz -- the two become close friends. As the world teeters on the brink of a nuclear war, Charles and Erik with other mutants join forces to save humanity. However, a situation soon tears the friends apart.

programme.title: Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri
programme.desc: After months have passed without a culprit in her daughter's murder case, Mildred Hayes makes a bold move, painting three signs leading into her town with a controversial message directed at William Willoughby, the town's revered chief of police. When his second-in-command, Officer Dixon -- an immature mother's boy with a penchant for violence -- gets involved, the battle is only exacerbated.

programme.title: Beirut

Meanwhile, a CIA field agent who is working undercover at the American embassy is tasked with keeping Mason alive and ensuring that the mission is a success.

programme.title: The Perfect Match
programme.desc: Charlie (Terrence J) is a charming playboy who doesn't believe in serious relationships. His best friends bet him that if he commits to one woman for one month, he's bound to fall in love. Charlie accepts the seemingly easy challenge, but wasn't expecting to cross paths with the beautiful and mysterious Eva (Cassie Ventura). When Charlie coaxes her into a casual affair, Eva turns the tables on him, forcing the lifelong bachelor to question whether he wants more than just a one-night stand.

programme.title: Spring Breakers
programme.desc: College students Candy (Vanessa Hudgens), Faith (Selena Gomez), Brit (Ashley Benson) and Cotty (Rachel Korine) are short of the cash they need for a spring-break trip, so they rob a diner and head down to Florida. However, the police soon break up the party and arrest them. The curvaceous quartet are unexpectedly bailed out by a drug dealer and aspiring rap artist named Alien (James Franco). Soon after, three of the four gal pals decide to join Alien in a life of crime.

programme.title: Get Him to the Greek
programme.desc: An ambitious executive at a record company, Aaron Green (Jonah Hill) gets what looks like an easy assignment: He must escort British rock legend Aldous Snow (Russell Brand) to L.A.'s Greek Theatre for the first stop on a lucrative comeback-concert tour. Snow, however, has different plans. Learning his true love is in California, the rocker vows to win her back before starting the tour, forcing Aaron to pull out all the stops to get Snow on stage in time.

programme.title: Rampage
programme.desc: Primatologist Davis Okoye shares an unshakable bond with George, an extraordinarily intelligent, silverback gorilla that's been in his care since birth. When a rogue genetic experiment goes wrong, it causes George, a wolf and a reptile to grow to a monstrous size. As the mutated beasts embark on a path of destruction, Okoye teams up with a discredited genetic engineer and the military to secure an antidote and prevent a global catastrophe.

programme.title: Wonka
programme.desc: Armed with nothing but a hatful of dreams, young chocolatier Willy Wonka manages to change the world, one delectable bite at a time.

programme.title: DC League of Super-Pets
programme.desc: Krypto the Super-Dog and Superman are inseparable best friends, sharing the same superpowers and fighting crime side by side in Metropolis. However, when the Man of Steel and the rest of the Justice League are kidnapped, Krypto must convince a ragtag group of animals to master their own newfound powers for a rescue mission.

programme.title: Shazam!
programme.desc: We all have a superhero inside of us -- it just takes a bit of magic to bring it out. In 14-year-old Billy Batson's case, all he needs to do is shout out one word to transform into the adult superhero Shazam. Still a kid at heart, Shazam revels in the new version of himself by doing what any other teen would do -- have fun while testing out his newfound powers. But he'll need to master them quickly before the evil Dr. Thaddeus Sivana can get his hands on Shazam's magical abilities.

programme.title: Shazam! Fury of the Gods
programme.desc: Bestowed with the powers of the gods, Billy Batson and his fellow foster kids are still learning how to juggle teenage life with their adult superhero alter egos. When a vengeful trio of ancient gods arrives on Earth in search of the magic stolen from them long ago, Shazam and his allies get thrust into a battle for their superpowers, their lives, and the fate of the world.

programme.title: Black Adam
programme.desc: In ancient Kahndaq, Teth Adam was bestowed the almighty powers of the gods. After using these powers for vengeance, he was imprisoned, becoming Black Adam. Nearly 5,000 years have passed, and Black Adam has gone from man to myth to legend. Now free, his unique form of justice, born out of rage, is challenged by modern-day heroes who form the Justice Society: Hawkman, Dr. Fate, Atom Smasher and Cyclone.

programme.title: The Flash
programme.desc: Worlds collide when the Flash uses his superpowers to travel back in time to change the events of the past. However, when his attempt to save his family inadvertently alters the future, he becomes trapped in a reality in which General Zod has returned, threatening annihilation. With no other superheroes to turn to, the Flash looks to coax a very different Batman out of retirement and rescue an imprisoned Kryptonian -- albeit not the one he's looking for.

programme.title: Adult Best Friends
programme.desc: Katie takes her best friend, Delaney, on a nostalgic trip to their childhood hometown to tell her she's getting married. Their journey soon takes some unexpected turns courtesy of a bizarre rental homeowner, a chance encounter with a former classmate, a bachelor party, and a few potential love interests.

programme.title: The Alto Knights
programme.desc: In the 1950s, notorious New York crime bosses Frank Costello and Vito Genovese vie for control of the city streets. Once the best of friends, petty jealousies and a series of betrayals place them on a deadly collision course that reshapes organized crime forever.

programme.title: Camp Hell
programme.desc: Horrific events plague a teen when his parents send him to a Christian camp.

programme.title: Bring Her Back
programme.desc: A brother and sister uncover a terrifying ritual at the secluded home of their new foster mother.

programme.title: Halloween H20: 20 Years Later
programme.desc: Two decades after surviving a massacre on October 31, 1978, former babysitter Laurie Strode finds herself hunted by persistent knife-wielder Michael Myers. Laurie now lives in Northern California under an assumed name, where she works as the headmistress of a private school. But it's not far enough to escape Myers, who soon discovers her whereabouts. As Halloween descends upon Laurie's peaceful community, a feeling of dread weighs upon her -- with good reason.

programme.title: Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers
programme.desc: This installment marks the return of the seemingly indestructible masked murderer Michael Myers (George P. Wilbur), who is targeting Tommy Doyle (Paul Stephen Rudd), a young man tied into the legacy of the killer and his connections with the Strode family. As the supernatural elements of Michael's macabre abilities are explored, his longtime adversary, Dr. Sam Loomis (Donald Pleasence), is also back in yet another attempt to stop the psychopath's brutal rampages.

programme.title: Halloween: Resurrection
programme.desc: He's back for more... When a group of teens wins a contest to spend a night in Michael Myers' childhood home to be broadcast live on the Internet, they believe they are in for a little fun and some free publicity. But things go frightfully wrong and the game turns into a struggle to make it out of the house alive.

programme.title: It's Kind of a Funny Story
programme.desc: Stressed by adolescence, 16-year-old Craig Gilner (Keir Gilchrist) checks himself into a mental-health clinic. Unfortunately, the youth wing is closed, so he must spend his mandated five-day stay with adults. One of them, Bobby (Zach Galifianakis), quickly becomes his mentor -- and protege, while Craig finds himself drawn to a fellow teen, Noelle (Emma Roberts), who just may be the cure he needs to forget an unrequited crush.

programme.title: A Thousand Words
programme.desc: Jack McCall (Eddie Murphy) is a selfish literary agent whose fast-talking ways allow him to close any deal. His next target is New Age guru Dr. Sinja (Cliff Curtis), but the savvy doctor sees right through Jack. A magical tree appears in Jack's yard, and, according to Dr. Sinja, the tree and Jack are connected; every time Jack says a word, a leaf falls from the tree. When the last leaf drops, Jack will die. With just a thousand leaves left, Jack must learn to curb his speech or he's a goner.

programme.title: Ocean's Eleven
programme.desc: Dapper Danny Ocean is a man of action. Less than 24 hours into his parole from a New Jersey penitentiary, the wry, charismatic thief is already rolling out his next plan. Following three rules: Don't hurt anybody, don't steal from anyone who doesn't deserve it, and play the game like you've got nothing to lose. Danny orchestrates the most sophisticated, elaborate casino heist in history.

programme.title: Ocean's Twelve
programme.desc: After successfully robbing five casinos in one night, Danny Ocean and his crew of thieves have big problems. Despite pulling off one of the biggest heists in Las Vegas history, the members of the gang have already spent much of the money they stole. Casino owner Terry Benedict demands that Ocean return the money, plus millions more in interest. Unable to come up the cash, the crew is forced to come together to pull off another series of heists, this time in Europe.

programme.title: Ocean's Thirteen
programme.desc: Danny Ocean and his gang hatch an ambitious plot for revenge after ruthless casino owner Willy Bank double-crosses Reuben Tishkoff, Danny's friend and mentor. First, Ocean's gang plan to hit Bank in the paycheck by reversing the precept that the house always wins. Next, they will deal a crushing blow to Bank's ego by ruining his reputation as the only hotelier to earn the Royal Review's Five Diamond Award for each of his properties.

programme.title: The Switch
programme.desc: Neurotic Wally Mars has one bright spot in his life: his friendship with Kassie. When Kassie announces her intention to become pregnant using a sperm donor, Wally thinks he will be the lucky guy, but Kassie has someone else in mind. While drunk at Kassie's insemination party, Wally substitutes his sperm for the donor's, then passes out, remembering nothing. Seven years later, Wally meets Kassie's son, who seems oddly familiar to him.

programme.title: Girls Trip

Along the way, they rekindle their sisterhood and rediscover their wild side by doing enough dancing, drinking, brawling and romancing to make the Big Easy blush.

programme.title: The Internship
